verdicts.evidence: Note line 66: "Terminal outcome | n/a (no attempt started) | Plan §7 classifier applies, incl. V05/V06 advisory semantics". SmartRouter 9b4bd68 (unchanged at ac59658) DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:104 defines separate axes, `execution_state` / `verification_status` / `recovery_status` / `accounting_status`, and says "completed means the requested subject work finished, not merely that a socket closed". :106: "A denied recommendation-generation call yields blocked; delivered advisory text with a demonstrated contract/safety violation yields failed; incomplete/unchecked advisory output yields unverified... V05-V06 exercise these boundaries." :110-115 give the six-outcome priority order. :300-301 are V05 and V06, the latter with "effect observed, charge pending". Moonzila 71436b5: src/shared/contracts.ts:15 is a single-axis `RunStatusSchema` ("completed", "failed", "cancelled", "interrupted", ...), backed by the CHECK constraint at src/engine/migrations.ts:32. src/engine/application.ts:364-368 marks a run completed when the provider outcome is "complete". :396 writes only run.cancelled or run.failed. src/engine/store.ts:398 writes run.interrupted. :229-230 rejects a policy violation by throwing before `putRun` (:236). contracts.ts:51 records usage as token counts only. The run.start request takes an explicit profileId (application.ts:229), and discovery-1.json reports that "selectLocal has no production caller".
verdicts.note: From SmartRouter's side the note is consistent: §7 explicitly covers advisory-only recommendation generation, and V05/V06 are its advisory fixtures. On the Moonzila side, applying the classifier is possible only as new design; the existing terminal-outcome handling cannot express it. (1) Moonzila has no generation attempt for a recommendation. Runs use a user-picked profile, and the selector is not wired. (2) Run state is one enum. It has no verification, recovery or accounting axes and no blocked, unverified, recommendation-only or accepted outcomes. Its "completed" means the provider stream ended with a stop, which is the transport-level success that §7 (:94, :104) rejects. (3) A policy-blocked request throws before any run row exists, so a §7 "blocked" record would have nowhere to live. (4) Accounting is token counts only, with no money, reservations or pending charges. So V06's "charge pending" and accounting_status have no source, and plan :368 says to simplify or stop when "accounting/dispatch absent". (5) V06 needs an observed-effects journal for unauthorized egress. Moonzila's design refuses egress before sending (assertRunPolicy, application.ts:472-475) rather than recording it. All of this would need a new contract and migration. A further caveat: SmartRouter's reference `classify_terminal` (tests/smart_router_decisions.py:195-211, added after 9b4bd68 and present at b6e04fd/ac59658) returns "recommendation only" for every advisory case that has no violation and no Stop. It ignores verification_status, so it would mislabel the denied-call (blocked) and unchecked (unverified) cases from plan :106. Its V05 call also passes verification_status="unverified", while plan :300 says "advisory verification accepted". Porting it as-is would not reproduce §7's advisory semantics.

summary:
Overall the plan points the right way, but Moonzila cannot build it as written. What it gets right: installed-app checks and source checks are kept apart, Report only is the default, nothing merges or publishes on its own, maintenance stays out of src/engine/scheduler.ts, and research comes first. The trouble is that from stage 3 on, the plan assumes things Moonzila does not have.

1. It assumes standing approval for check commands. Moonzila only has exact, per-command approval that is used once (src/main/commands.ts:103-112).
2. It assumes write containment for repair and break-test workspaces. The only containment is a Job Object with kill-on-close (native/host.cpp:119-122) plus a cwd-only protected-root check (src/main/commands.ts:84-85).
3. It assumes the checkout under test is separate from the app that is running. In a source run they are the same folder: scripts/build.mjs:5 deletes dist/, which src/main/index.ts:153 loads the engine from.

It also ignores recorded user decisions in the research-jobs plan (HEAD 71436b5, lines 458-469). Those decisions put heavy and Windows-only checks on GitHub Actions runners, require the user to approve every break-test, say that background work never bypasses exact command approval, and say that interrupted tasks are never re-run silently.

What is safe to build now, with existing pieces:
- A manual, report-only installed-app check that reads the app version, the interrupted-run and unknown-operation records (src/engine/store.ts:382-399) and which tools are present.
- A Full check that dispatches the existing `Windows verification` workflow (.github/workflows/windows.yml:5) and shows its result, following the collector's dispatch-once pattern (src/main/collector.ts:79-85).

Everything after that first needs new pieces: a sandbox, a schema v5 record, a policy holder, and Stage F (signing, update feed, quiescence, backups).
strengths: Separating the installed-app check from the developer self-test matches what the installer actually ships. It ships only dist/** and package.json inside an asar (electron-builder.yml:5-9), with onlyLoadAppFromAsar on (:22), so an installed copy cannot run the suite (MZ-27, MZ-46).

Keeping maintenance out of src/engine/scheduler.ts is right. Its 'maintenance' kind stops the model runtime and refuses new inference (scheduler.ts:65-71: `if (kind === 'inference' && this.maintenance) throw new Error('RUNTIME_MAINTENANCE')`). Reusing it would break the plan's own rule in section 7.

The default policy matches existing rules. Report only by default, with no silent replacement, merge or release, matches 'Moonzila never merges' (research-jobs plan HEAD:421), G22 (docs/specification/source-plan.md:124) and the merge checks in AGENTS.md:19.

Recording a missed run and retrying it at the next start is the cheapest safe first version. It fits the existing startup-reconciliation pattern: CollectorSupervisor.attach (src/main/collector.ts:110-111) and research.recover once per start (src/main/index.ts:134-135).
Reporting environment failures as Blocked and comparing against a baseline is the repository's own practice: AGENTS.md:60-64 (74-test Linux set, numTotalTests and files with no assertion results).

The plan makes research an explicit stage before choosing any Windows scheduling, signing, update or rollback mechanism. None of the 18 corpora under docs/research covers these topics (MZ-22), and AGENTS.md:33 requires research first.

Its account of where Moonzila stands is accurate. Diagnostics, updates, signing and wider installed-app qualification are listed as unfinished (HANDOFF.md:48, :88; docs/development-status.md:172), and break-test exists only as a skill (AGENTS.md:29).

problems.problem: Scheduled Full checks and the 'approved, allowlisted check commands' amount to a standing approval to run whatever code the checkout holds at that moment. An allowlist of command names (`npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm run build`) does not limit what runs: lifecycle scripts, vitest and Playwright configs, every test file and scripts/*.mjs all come from the repository. This conflicts with approval binding, with G13, and with the recorded rule that background work never bypasses exact command approval. If Moonzila reads `.github/workflows/windows.yml` from the checkout to decide what to run, repository content would be granting command execution, which G10 and G24 forbid.

summary:
Verdict: most of the plan's principles fit Moonzila's rules and should be recorded as decisions now. As a build plan, though, it should not be adopted as written. It is a new feature in no recorded order, and it partly re-plans work that is already queued.

The plan has two halves:
- **Developer self-test** (stages 4-5 and the Full check). This repeats three things already decided: Self-unblocking (blocked run, self-fix, research, a PR that Moonzila never merges, then notify), the break-test preset in missions, and background tasks. It also contradicts the recorded decision that checks and break-tests run on GitHub Actions runners, not the user's PC (research-jobs.md:466).
- **Installed-app check** (§1, Quick check, stage 6). This depends almost entirely on unbuilt Stage F work (F1 updates and backups, F2 diagnostics, F3 signing) and on external inputs nobody has supplied yet (source-plan.md:3812-3814). A stage-2 report today could cover only the environment probes that already exist and the interrupted-run records.

On More models: the plan does not need it until stage 5, when AI patch proposals start. At that point there is no local model on the user's PC, and no cloud preset is offered until its tool-call test (U-06) passes. So patch proposals depend on More models' first build step, and they raise questions about cloud spend and code disclosure that a schedule must not answer unattended.

Rough cost of the whole plan: about the size of the research-jobs phase (PRs #20-#37; about 3.7k source lines across the research modules, part of it older than that phase; 26 research test files, about 7.2k lines), and stages 5-6 also need external inputs.

Recommended order: nothing before More models' Mandate (RUN.md:27,42). Record the principles as decisions. Fold the installed-app check into Stage F2 diagnostics. Make the Full check a GitHub `workflow_dispatch` run of `windows.yml`. Route patch proposals through Self-unblocking. Build scheduling once, as a general scheduled-background-task capability in the missions phase.

Line numbers for research-jobs.md refer to the uncommitted working tree; at HEAD b490e50, lines after 402 are 4 lower.
strengths: Splitting the installed-app check from the developer self-test matches the packaging. The installer ships only dist/** and package.json inside an asar (electron-builder.yml:5-9, :22), so a full test run can only exist next to a source checkout.

'Report only' is the default, and no AI patch becomes an update just because a test passed. This matches AGENTS.md:8 (never manufacture release evidence), decisions.md:8 (verification cannot self-certify) and Self-unblocking's 'Moonzila never merges' (research-jobs.md:425).

It keeps maintenance out of src/engine/scheduler.ts. Its 'maintenance' entry kind stops the model runtime and refuses new inference (scheduler.ts:65-71, :156-157), so reusing it would break the plan's own rule in §7 that a check must not interrupt inference.

The first version handles a closed app by recording the missed run and running at the next start, with no OS-level scheduler. This matches main's existing reconcile-at-start pattern (src/main/index.ts:134-135; src/engine/index.ts:15) and the rule in operate-mode.md:25 that a desktop app which sleeps must not be the process that keeps something alive.
It names the Windows CI workflow as the source of truth instead of an improvised command list. That matches AGENTS.md:42, where that workflow is the acceptance gate.
It reports environment gaps separately from defects. Moonzila's gate already works this way (AGENTS.md:61-64: the 74-test Linux baseline, the numTotalTests comparison and the files with no results).
Trusted repair comes last in the stages, only after the release path supports verification. This matches the Stage F order: quiescence, backup, signing (source-plan.md:3333-3582).
It is honest about its own limits: no code was changed, Research-Kit was not available to its author, and the Windows details are to be researched, not guessed.

decisionsForOwner: Q1 - When, and in which shape? Options: (a) start Maintenance now; (b) build it whole after More models, before Self-unblocking and project memory; (c) split it: the installed-app health check joins Stage F2 diagnostics, and the developer parts go inside Self-unblocking and missions. Recommendation: (c), with nothing built before More models' Mandate (RUN.md:27, :42). Meanwhile record the plan's principles as decisions in research-jobs.md.

Q2 - Where does the Full check run? Options: (a) locally in the app, replaying windows.yml's commands; (b) dispatch windows.yml on GitHub at an exact ref and read the conclusion; (c) both. Recommendation: (b). It matches your October 2 decision (research-jobs.md:466) and AGENTS.md:11. It needs a GitHub connection with permission to dispatch Actions on StepenkoAnatoli/MoonAliza, the same step 1 that Self-unblocking needs (research-jobs.md:464).

Q3 - May a scheduled run call a model, spend credits, or start a break-test while you are away? Options: (a) never: schedules run deterministic checks only, and anything else starts from the report when you click, with cost and destination shown; (b) a standing opt-in with a budget. Recommendation: (a). It matches 'the user approves every break-test run, with its cost shown' (research-jobs.md:462) and the 'permission at call time' rule in the advisory note.

Q4 - Where does a proposed fix go? Options: (a) a diff shown only inside the app; (b) a branch and draft PR on MoonAliza that Moonzila never merges, as Self-unblocking already fixes. Recommendation: (b), built as part of Self-unblocking. The fix counts only when CI is green on the PR head and an independent verifier agrees, not on the patching run's own proof (decisions.md:8).

Q5 - Which privacy policy governs sending Moonzila's own source and test output to a cloud model? Options: (a) the Moonzila checkout must be opened as a trusted project, and its project policy applies; (b) a new app-wide maintenance policy. Recommendation: (a), and only to vendors in the shortlist's 'offerable for private code' class (coding-model-shortlist BRIEF.md:348-367).

Q6 - Should 'Developer mode' exist? Options: (a) a new global mode or setting; (b) none: the developer self-test is available when you open the Moonzila checkout as a project yourself, and the app never searches the disk for it. Recommendation: (b).

Q7 - What may 'repair the installed app' do before signed releases exist? Options: (a) report only, with a link to the release page, until F1 and F3; (b) reinstall the same version; (c) restore any older version, with a database backup. Recommendation: (a). Decide the production signing inputs once, for both purposes: the Authenticode identity and an Ed25519 key for a release manifest and More models' catalogue. Both are external inputs (source-plan.md:3812-3814).

Q8 - Where are maintenance records and schedule options stored? Options: (a) a new engine table, taking the schema step after project memory's v5; (b) main-owned, bounded files, as collector settings and the research spool do, with no schema step. Recommendation: (b) if a report-only slice ships before memory, otherwise (a). Never add schedule fields to the strict SettingsSchema without a schema step, because an older build would fail at every run start (application.ts:157-159, :329).

Q9 - One scheduler or two? Options: (a) a coordinator only for maintenance; (b) a general 'scheduled background task' capability in the background-tasks part of missions, also serving the dependency watch (research-jobs.md:525). Recommendation: (b).

Q10 - Should a check interrupted by app exit run again at the next start? Options: (a) yes, automatically; (b) no: it shows as interrupted, as background tasks do (research-jobs.md:472), and only a missed due time starts one new run, if you turned that on. Recommendation: (b).

Q11 - Names: keep 'Maintenance' and 'Blocked' / 'Needs review'? Recommendation: rename to 'Health check', with statuses Passed / Failed / Could not run (environment) / Skipped / Unverified. The current words already mean other things in the scheduler, Research-Kit, project memory and the Changes and Recovery panels.

Rough cost, for deciding: a report-only health-check slice is about 8-12 files (contract and params, bridge messages, a main coordinator, engine-exit and crash recording, storage, a panel and its entry, architecture and spec docs), 0-1 schema steps, 4-6 test files and 1 e2e journey. That is comparable to one research-jobs task. Scheduling adds 3-5 files and fake-clock tests. A local break-test or repair workspace is a new security design, larger than the owned-collection task; on CI it is mostly a dispatch-and-watch client like the collector. Patch proposals are the Self-unblocking phase. Trusted repair and updates are F1 + F3 + F5 plus external inputs.

summary: Judged against Moonzila as it is at b490e50/71436b5 (src unchanged), the note's core display-versus-generate split fits Moonzila's process architecture, but most of the fields and bindings it asks for have no source in Moonzila. What fits: Path A can be inference-free by construction. Engine read methods touch only SQLite (src/engine/application.ts:136-155), and every network effect is a main-process hook (src/main/index.ts:85-122). Secret exclusion is already enforced: the vault is main-only, secretRef is stripped from DTOs, credential URLs are refused and model output is redacted. Every dispatch already re-checks the live policy at admission and before and after each step, so a stored preview cannot become a dispatch pass. What does not fit: Moonzila has no price list, no capability/catalogue or verifier revision, no model or tool-config revision, no skill runtime, no money accounting and no per-call grant for inference. Locality is inferred from the endpoint host. Three requirements are unsafe or cannot be met if built as written. (1) "Path B uses the canonical skill semantics" can only mean skill text inside a model prompt here, so Gate 1 (privacy) would be judged after the bytes are already sent. (2) Path A's validity rule binds to revisions that do not exist, so either nothing is ever valid or constant revisions get invented. (3) "Explicit permission at call time" has nowhere to live: approvals are bound to operations and need a project, and method authorization labels are never enforced. Further important gaps: the renderer "proof-of-no-inference" counter cannot see egress; a display event cannot be stored in the run-scoped event log; showing stale previews contradicts Moonzila's rule of withholding unverified content; "local" as a privacy destination is not verified; Path B would be a model dispatch, so it must be a run with Stop, recovery and the project lock. Recommendation: do not adopt the note as an implementation spec. Carry its four structural rules (separate paths, no inference on display, stale invalidation, no secret-bearing records) into the More models direction-3 design as requirements, with the gates checked in host code. Adoption is a decision for the More models Mandate, which still waits for the user.
strengths: Path A can have zero egress by construction, not only by a promise. Engine read methods (src/engine/application.ts:136-155) read only the Store, src/engine contains no fetch call, and every model call or fetch is a main hook (src/main/index.ts:85-122 infer/readGitHub, wired at :154-177). An engine `read` method for stored previews cannot reach a provider.

The no-secrets rule for records is already a Moonzila invariant, enforced in code. The vault is main-process only and grants are bound to epoch, purpose, context and profile revision (src/main/vault.ts:24-25, :129-141). publicProfile strips secretRef (src/engine/application.ts:130-135). HttpUrlSchema refuses embedded credentials (src/shared/contracts.ts:10-12) and validateEndpoint refuses user, query and fragment (src/main/inference.ts:17). Model output and tool calls are redacted in main before they reach the engine (src/main/index.ts:102-106), and redaction fails closed (vault.ts:183-195).

"A stored recommendation must never become a free dispatch pass" already holds. Dispatch happens only through run.start, which runs assertConversationPolicy at admission (application.ts:230) and again before and after every model step (application.ts:356, 362, via assertRunPolicy at :472). Main runs it again before sending any bytes (src/main/index.ts:88-93). It is covered by tests/application.test.ts:74 ('cloud policy blocks network admission and persists no user prompt').

The stale-authority pattern already exists for runs and approvals. Each run pins sessionPolicyRevision, policyRevision, trustRevision and profileRevisionId (contracts.ts:28), and a mismatch refuses (policy.ts:75-76). Approvals bind inputHash plus the policy and trust revisions (policy.ts:35-41). Revoking trust increments trustRevision and aborts runs (application.ts:213-216; main/index.ts:201-211). A preview can reuse the same compare-on-read check.

The advisory-only boundary matches reality. The user picks a profile for each run (App.tsx:236; application.ts:229). There is no routing or selection tool: the model.* methods fall through to NOT_IMPLEMENTED (application.ts:265), and selectLocal has no caller.

There is a base for binding. Profile revisions are immutable and stored as history (migrations.ts:17-24; store.ts:155-165 'Profile revision is immutable'). canonicalHash hashes exact JSON without whitespace folding (policy.ts:44-65), which fits S16 for the bytes it actually receives.

The note correctly leaves schema, storage and UI routing to Moonzila. It also says written notes do not satisfy runtime gates, which matches Moonzila's 'completion is counted, never estimated' (research-jobs.md, Decisions recorded October 2).

problems.problem: Path B 'must use the canonical skill semantics' with 'Gate 1 checked before any transmission'. In Moonzila the only way to apply a skill is to put its text in a model's context. The gates would then be judged by the model after the task, policy and profile data have already been sent to it, so Gate 1 could never run before transmission.
problems.evidence: SmartRouter SKILL.md:33-34 @9b4bd68: 'check **before** any fetch, cache write, embedding or transmission'. SKILL.md:20-22: 'Target hosts must own actual authorization, model identity/dispatch, privacy enforcement and billing'. Moonzila skills are instruction text loaded into a run (docs/specification/source-plan.md:2177-2205, Task C3: 16 KiB bodies, at most three per run, 'Skills cannot change permissions'), and no loader exists (skill.list falls to NOT_IMPLEMENTED, src/engine/application.ts:265). The only pre-send gate is host code: assertConversationPolicy (src/engine/policy.ts:68-79) at application.ts:230/356 and main/index.ts:90.
problems.recommendation: Run every gate whose inputs the host can observe (privacy and destination, profile kind and credential, policy and trust revisions, run admission) as deterministic engine/main code before the generating call, and record each verdict as a code. The skill text may inform only the difficulty and economics judgement. Never treat model-produced gate text as a verdict (SmartRouter Gate 3: 'self-scores are not acceptance'; Moonzila decision 8: verification 'cannot self-certify', decisions.md:12).

problems.problem: Path A's validity condition cannot be met in Moonzila. §3.1 requires matching authority, price, catalogue and verifier revisions. Price-list, capability/catalogue and verifier-contract revisions do not exist, and under SmartRouter's own rule unknown evidence invalidates the route. Built as written, either no preview is ever valid or the builder invents constant revisions, which is manufactured evidence. Separately, §3.1 lists exactly the revisions Moonzila lacks and leaves out the ones it has (session policy, project policy and trust, profile revision); §3.4 lists both. summary:
Verdict: the note accurately states four SmartRouter rules, but it is the wrong piece of work for Moonzila to take on now. It should not become a separate task. Use it as a set of constraints on More models direction 3 and settle it at the More models Mandate. RUN.md:27 already holds the note for that decision.

Why it does not fit Moonzila's queue:

1. It is not on Moonzila's roadmap, and it competes with selection work already queued or approved. No committed Moonzila file mentions it. The competing items are:
   - direction 3 "Smarter selection" (research-jobs.md:410);
   - the user-approved mission planner, which picks a profile per agent and fills an approval card (research-jobs.md:385-390);
   - the "three model roles" first build step in the pricing brief (2026-10-02 pricing BRIEF:112);
   - Stage C "improve actionable profile selection" (development-status.md:83);
   - G08, automatic model selection (source-plan.md:110).
   
   Line numbers for research-jobs.md are from the working tree; from "More models" on they are 4 lower at HEAD 71436b5.

2. SmartRouter's own plan argues against approving it now:
   - Conflicting selection authorities must stop work until reconciled (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:50 @9b4bd68).
   - The plan says to simplify or stop when accounting or dispatch is absent (:368), and Moonzila has no accounting.
   - The §13 acceptance needs measured benefit (:352). SmartRouter has not measured it: PHASE4_PILOT_REPORT.md:90-92 @ac59658 says costs were not measured and calls itself "a coverage ledger, not a comparative measurement".

3. The order is backwards. Each of the six §13 display fields needs something More models has not built yet, so an advisory UI built first would show wrong or unknown values:
   - Privacy destination: today it is a loopback host check (inference.ts:18-20), which a loopback Ollama serving cloud models defeats (wire-formats BRIEF:522). Vendor data-use classes exist only in shortlist BRIEF:348.
   - Dispatch availability: needs the direction-2 adapters and the U-06 tool-call receipts (shortlist BRIEF:408-413).
   - Cost basis: no code holds any price; prices exist only in a dated research table (pricing BRIEF:86-110).

4. The note assumes Moonzila capabilities that do not exist:
   - Path A (show a stored preview) has nothing to show: nothing produces previews, and three of the four revisions its validity check compares (price, catalogue, verifier) do not exist.
   - Path B (generate a new recommendation) needs:
     - a call-time grant: today only for edits and commands; the `user-confirmed` rule is never enforced;
     - a skill runtime;
     - accounting;
     - outcome axes beyond the single run status;
     - a log of display and generate events that is not tied to a run.

   On the user's PC, Path B could never run in a local-only project, because no local model fits in memory.

Recommendation:
- Adopt the four plan-backed rules as constraints on direction 3.
- Build the advisory surface as an eligibility display beside the profile picker. It would be recomputed on every view and use no model calls: no stored previews, no generate path, so nothing can go stale.
- Keep Moonzila's own deterministic selector as the only selection authority.

decisionsForOwner: Should Moonzila approve SmartRouter's advisory UI note? (a) Approve it as-is, which opens a SmartRouter Phase 6 task. (b) Approve only its four plan-backed rules as constraints on Moonzila's own model-selection work: display separate from generate, no inference on display, invalidation when authority goes stale, no secrets in records. Decline the rest: stored previews, Path B, the field list and the UI counter. (c) Decline it. Recommendation: (b), recorded as a dated decision with its rejected alternative under the More models plan entry, and answered at the More models Mandate, where RUN.md:27 already holds the question.

Which component is Moonzila's single model-selection authority? (a) The SmartRouter canonical skill. (b) Moonzila's deterministic selector: selectLocal (src/models/select.ts), extended by direction 3 and later by the mission planner (research-jobs.md:385-390). (c) Both, reconciled by a written decision. Recommendation: (b). SmartRouter forbids two authorities (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:50), Moonzila already has G08 and an approved mission planner, and the skill has no runtime in Moonzila. SmartRouter's five gates can serve as the checklist for the selector's displayed reasons.

Where does an advisory surface go in the queue? (a) As its own task now, before More models Stage 2. (b) Inside More models direction 3, after the direction 2 groundwork including the fail-closed locality rule (wire-formats BRIEF:560-575) and after the cloud preset table with U-06 receipts (shortlist BRIEF:408-413). (c) After missions. Recommendation: (b) for a display that makes no model calls; anything model-generated waits until after missions.

Should recommendations be stored or recomputed? (a) Store preview records bound to revisions, which needs a schema step (v6, after memory's v5) and invalidation logic. (b) Recompute eligibility and reasons on every display from current state and store nothing. Recommendation: (b). Nothing produces stored previews, three of the four binding revisions do not exist, and the note allows re-derivation (note:83).

Should the first stage include model-generated recommendations (Path B)? (a) Yes, by running the SmartRouter skill on a chosen profile. (b) Yes, through a deterministic port of the gates that makes no model calls, with difficulty supplied by the user. (c) No. Recommendation: (c) now; (b) inside direction 3 only if a difficulty input is wanted. Option (a) needs the C3 skill runtime, a call-time grant, accounting and new outcome axes. SmartRouter itself defers a paid classifier (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:427), and on this PC no local model fits for local-only projects (shortlist BRIEF:335).

If generation is ever built, what counts as the explicit call-time grant? (a) The user's click on Generate, after a preflight that names the destination profile, what is sent and 'cost unknown', under the existing cloud policy, the same way Send works (tests/workbench.test.tsx:55). (b) A per-call approval card bound the way operations are (src/engine/operations.ts:116-126), which needs a run and a project. (c) The policy setting alone. Recommendation: (a), never generate in the background, and in local-only projects require a qualified local profile.

What is the 'cost basis' source? (a) A dated static price table from docs/research/2026-10-02-model-pricing-and-ranking, using its retrieval date as the price-list revision and shown as an estimate. (b) OpenRouter's live models endpoint, which the shortlist brief allows only as a drift check (shortlist BRIEF:136). (c) Always 'unknown'. Recommendation: (a), labelled as an estimate and never presented as accounting, re-collected quarterly as that brief requires (pricing BRIEF:116), with 'unknown' wherever a row is missing.

Does Moonzila want strict spend caps? Caps would make SmartRouter's Gate 4 a blocker and need accounting and reservations, which is SmartRouter's §13 next stage. Options: caps now; disclosure only now, with caps considered alongside missions; never. Recommendation: disclosure only now, and revisit with missions, which already carry step budgets (research-jobs.md:383).

In what order should the queued tasks run? Recommendation: More models first (direction 2 groundwork, then cloud presets and U-06, then the fail-closed locality fix, then direction 3 with the eligibility display). Then the P4-23 linked-parent guard, before direction 1, because the model store, downloads and runtime use that guard (research-jobs.md:416). Then project memory (schema v5). Then Self-unblocking, reusing memory's lessons and SmartRouter §7's blocked/failed/unverified wording for 'cannot solve'. Then missions. Already decided by the user: More models first (RUN.md:42) and memory before missions (research-jobs.md:449). The rest is my recommendation.

May a displayed recommendation pre-fill the profile picker? (a) Yes; Send remains the only dispatch, and the existing re-checks still apply (src/main/index.ts:90; application.ts:230). (b) No, display only. Recommendation: (a). Pre-filling is a user action, not SmartRouter's 'manual eligible overrides' stage (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:348), because run.start and main re-check policy regardless.
